pr_body:
/kind feature
/sig scheduling
/priority important-soon
/hold

**What this PR does / why we need it**:

Per discussion in https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/1178, we'll

1. Expand the original range to [0, 100] 
2. Return an error when score plugins returns a score which is out of range [0, 100]

Not sure what you mean by "broken change", we are not changing the name of the variable, it will require an API review though. What concerns me the most is that we will be using a different range than what the API advertises.

Perhaps we shouldn't change the range in this PR, this PR is about enforcing the range only.

> Not sure what you mean by "broken change", we are not changing the name of the variable, it will require an API review though. What concerns me the most is that we will be using a different range than what the API advertises.

`MaxPriority` defined is in the `pkg/scheduler/api/types.go` file which is exposed by the scheduler, the developer could use it to do some calculation, if we change the value of `MaxPriority`, it may break the developers' code. Does that make sense to you?

> Perhaps we shouldn't change the range in this PR, this PR is about enforcing the range only.

I could split this PR but I don't see its necessity.

> > Not sure what you mean by "broken change", we are not changing the name of the variable, it will require an API review though. What concerns me the most is that we will be using a different range than what the API advertises.
> 
> `MaxPriority` defined is in the `pkg/scheduler/api/types.go` file which is exposed by the scheduler, the developer could use it to do some calculation, if we change the value of `MaxPriority`, it may break the developers' code. Does that make sense to you?
> 

The variable name (MaxPriority) we define in the API and its semantics (that it represents the maximum priority) is our contract with the developers, not the exact value. We certainly need to be careful when changing it though. What I would like to understand is why this is part of the scheduler API?

> > Perhaps we shouldn't change the range in this PR, this PR is about enforcing the range only.
> 
> I could split this PR but I don't see its necessity.

We need to understand better the implications of changing the range, especially that the constant is part of the API. For example, do we need to make the new constant (MaxNodeScore) part of the API? Do we need to roll it out under a feature flag? For those reasons I prefer to have a dedicated Issue (so that it is well advertised) and PR for the range change that we can reference in the future as well.

Scaling up the priority may be the best path forward depending on who is using MaxPriority API and how we decide to roll out the range change, this is a discussion we can have on the issue, but at the least I think it shouldn't be done in such an obscure way (multiplying explicitly by 10), we at least need to define a function/constant that is computed from MaxPriority and MaxNodeScore: ```Multiplier := MaxNodeScore/MaxPriority```

> What I would like to understand is why this is part of the scheduler API?

As I mentioned before It is exposed in the scheduler API which could be used by the developers who import the scheduler API packages and use them to create a scheduler extender.

> I prefer to have a dedicated Issue (so that it is well advertised)

This is an internal change and totally compatible (forward and backwards) the developers won't feel it, I still don't see the necessity, but I'll create an issue for advertising and further discussion https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/81281.

> For example, do we need to make the new constant (MaxNodeScore) part of the API?

The new constant has to be part of the API since the user should be aware of the maximum node score so that they could enforce the range which returned by the scoring plugin.

> Do we need to roll it out under a feature flag?

As bobby mentioned https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/1178#issuecomment-519197118, these are **internal functions**, we could change them to provide a fine-grained range.

> MaxPriority and MaxNodeScore: Multiplier := MaxNodeScore/MaxPriority

SG

cc/ @bsalamat

It seems to me that the current `MaxPriority` plays a similar role as the newly introduced `NodeScoreMax`, and the current [`NormalizeReduce`](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/1fe7ce21bcf73c0a82811c75afb12254488adfaa/pkg/scheduler/algorithm/priorities/reduce.go#L54) function normalizes score results to be in the range of [0, `MaxPriority`]. Am I correct on this?

With this change, how do we expect `MaxPriority` and `NodeScoreMax` to play together? And is there any documentation to clarify this for developers?

> the current NormalizeReduce function normalizes score results to be in the range of [0, MaxPriority].

No, it should be in the range of [0, MaxNodeScore]

> With this change, how do we expect `MaxPriority` and `NodeScoreMax` to play together? And is there any documentation to clarify this for developers?

As I mentioned above multiple times, this is an internal change and totally compatible (forward and backwards) the developers won't feel it. They are two different modules and we can make it compatible in the kubernetes codebase.

> > What I would like to understand is why this is part of the scheduler API?
> 
> As I mentioned before It is exposed in the scheduler API which could be used by the developers who import the scheduler API packages and use them to create a scheduler extender.
> 

You mentioned that before, but it is not a good enough answer. We need to understand why the scheduler and whatever other thing that imports its API needed to share the same MaxPriority. If as you say the extenders are the ones use it, then we need to understand why: for example, are they sending a reply back that the scheduler expects to be in the [0, MaxPriority] range, if yes, are we handling that reply properly now that we are changing the range to [0, 100]?

> > I prefer to have a dedicated Issue (so that it is well advertised)
> 
> This is an internal change and totally compatible (forward and backwards) the developers won't feel it, I still don't see the necessity, but I'll create an issue for advertising and further discussion #81281.

Thanks

> 
> The new constant has to be part of the API since the user should be aware of the maximum node score so that they could enforce the range which returned by the scoring plugin.

Yes, the developers should use the const in the scheduler API to enforce the range, but we cannot stop them from using a hard-coded `100` as well.

> You mentioned that before, but it is not a good enough answer. We need to understand why the scheduler and whatever other thing that imports its API needed to share the same MaxPriority. If as you say the extenders are the ones use it, then we need to understand why: for example, are they sending a reply back that the scheduler expects to be in the [0, MaxPriority] range, if yes, are we handling that reply properly now that we are changing the range to [0, 100]?

issue_context.title: Enforce the range of score returned by the score plugin
issue_context.body:
**What would you like to be added**:

1. Add a default normalize score function in the scheduling framework.
2. Skip the plugin and log an error when the normalizing phase returns an invalid range of scores.

**Why is this needed**:

Per discussion in https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/1178, we should enforce the range of score returned by the scoring plugin.

/sig scheduling
/priority important-soon
/assign

review_comments:
I think we should also send an error over the `errCh`. We currently ignore a faulty plugin and only log a message. These log messages may remain unnoticed for a while. I would prefer a more serious action, like not scheduling the pod so that a cluster admin notices the issue.
If you decided to go with my suggestion, you may want to remove the `klog.Errorf` above and only send an error message over `errCh`.
